summary: Live-API acceptance of the 2-tier Triage → Magnum DI contract plus mobile smoke of Check / Call Guard / Patrol detail. 9/9 live backend tests pass (tests/test_triage_live_api.py). Benign SMS → caseId null, geminiCalls 0, outcome NO_THREAT_IDENTIFIED. Scam SMS ('verification code to unlock') → one caseId, outcome POSSIBLE_THREAT_IDENTIFIED, rulesMet contains MSG-01, idempotency verified (same submission_id → same case). POST /api/call/risk-check still returns a reputation decision. Every triage outcome is now visible via GET /api/patrol/events with adapter_label 'Apollo Triage (deterministic)' and full triage_investigation payload (rulesApplicable/rulesChecked/rulesMet/coverageGaps/retries/correlation/reason/geminiCalls=0). Frontend home/Call Guard/Patrol detail routes render with no red-screen errors.

critical.issue: The PatrolEvent response_model was missing a triage_investigation field, so even though services/triage/store.py writes the full deterministic record into Mongo, Pydantic serialization stripped it from the HTTP response for ALL three outcomes (NO_THREAT / LIMITED / POSSIBLE_THREAT). Frontend had no way to display triage rulesChecked/coverageGaps/retries. Fixed by adding `triage_investigation: Optional[dict]` to PatrolEventIn in /app/backend/core/models.py and restarting backend. Verified by live test.

action_items: Review and keep the PatrolEvent.triage_investigation field (core/models.py). Confirm this doesn't need to be mirrored into PatrolEventPatch (currently read-only server-projected — correct).

Consider also surfacing the inner rulesMet/coverageGaps at the top-level of the POST /investigations/background/text 'triage' object; today the deterministic record lives under `triage.investigation.*`, which required test adaptation. The outer object only exposes outcome / reason / cached / source_type / providers_used / geminiCalls. Frontend TriageSummary already reads from `.investigation.*`, so this is a documentation note, not a bug.
critical_code_review_comments: services/triage/store.py correctly persists the full investigation wire into patrol_events.triage_investigation and into the dedicated triage_investigations collection — both are written for every outcome and idempotent on (device_id, investigation_id).

routers/investigations.py background_text_intake() flow is correct: _record_triage_history is called for the non-escalating path AND for the escalating path (with investigation_case_id bound). geminiCalls=0 is a hard-coded property of TriageResult.wire() — safe.

core/models.py: because PatrolEventIn is also used as the client submission schema (POST /patrol/events), consider marking triage_investigation as server-only via an explicit guard in routers/patrol.py upsert_event. Today a malicious client could submit a bogus triage_investigation payload. Not exploited in tests but worth hardening.
seed_data_creation: Each test registers its own anonymous device via /api/devices/register. No persistent seed. Patrol events created during tests are left in Mongo (short-lived test devices).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Live backend 2-tier triage flow is green end-to-end. The one bug found (triage_investigation stripped from /patrol/events response) was fixed in core/models.py and verified. If main agent regresses PatrolEventIn or renames the triage_investigation field, these tests will immediately fail.
rca_of_issue: Root cause: triage_investigation was written to Mongo by services/triage/store.py but PatrolEventIn (which backs the response_model of GET /patrol/events) did not declare the field, so FastAPI/Pydantic stripped it during serialization. Reproduction before fix: POST /api/investigations/background/text with any text → GET /api/patrol/events?device_id=... → event present with adapter_label 'Apollo Triage (deterministic)' but no triage_investigation key. Mitigation: Optional[dict] = None added to PatrolEventIn.
